\section{Threshold Functions --- Low Degree Norm}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.LowDegreeNorm
\subsection*{Threshold Functions --- Low Degree Norm: Introduction}
Hypercontractive moment bounds and interpolation compare the first and second moments of low-degree Walsh polynomials with the sharp exponential degree factor.

\subsection*{Threshold Functions --- Low Degree Norm: Results}

\begin{lemma}[Noise lower bound for low-degree energy]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.noise_degree_lower}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noise_l2_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.fourierCoeff_eval, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, and let $p$ be a real coefficient family on the subsets of $[n]$
that vanishes on every subset of size greater than $k$. For $0\le\rho\le1$, the noise
operator applied to the Boolean-cube function represented by $p$ satisfies
\[
\rho^{2k}\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}p(S)^2\le \mathbb E\!\left[(T_\rho P_p)^2\right],
\]
where the expectation is uniform on the cube.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Low degree moment bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.low_degree_moment_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_rpow_abs_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_sq_noiseOp_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.general_one_function_hypercontractivity, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.noise_degree_lower, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n,k$ be natural numbers, let $p$ be a coefficient family on subsets of the $n$
coordinates, and suppose $p(S)=0$ whenever $|S|>k$. For every real $t$ with $1<t<2$,
writing $P(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}p(S)\chi_S(x)$, one has
$\displaystyle(t-1)^k\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}p(S)^2\leq\left(\mathbb
E_{x\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\{0,1\}^n)}|P(x)|^t\right)^{2/t}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Interpolation between first and second moments]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.moment_interpolation}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.expect_eq_fintypeExpect}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let
$t\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $1<t<2$. With expectation taken under the uniform measure on the
Boolean cube, $$\E[|f|^t]\leq \E[|f|]^{2-t}\E[f^2]^{t-1}.$$
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Power form of the interpolation bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.interp_pow}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $m\in\mathbb N$ and $A,B,M\in\mathbb R$ be nonnegative. If $M\le
A^{1/(m+1)}B^{m/(m+1)}$, where these are real powers, then $M^{2(m+1)}\le A^2B^{2m}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Natural-power form of a moment comparison]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.hc_pow}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $m,k$ be natural numbers and let $B,M,D$ be nonnegative real numbers. If $D^kB\leq
M^{2(m+1)/(2m+1)}$, then $(D^kB)^{2m+1}\leq M^{2(m+1)}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Algebraic cancellation inequality]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.abstract_cancel}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $m,k$ be nonnegative integers and $A,B,M,C,D$ be real numbers. Suppose $B>0$, $C\ge
1$, $CD=1$, $(D^kB)^{2m+1}\le M^{2(m+1)}$, and $M^{2(m+1)}\le A^2B^{2m}$. Then $B\le
(C^{m+1})^{2k}A^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Finite exponential degree bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.finite_algebra}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.abstract_cancel, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.hc_pow, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.interp_pow}
\difficulty{4}
Let $m,k$ be nonnegative integers with $m\ge1$, and let $A,M\in\mathbb R$ be nonnegative
and $B\in\mathbb R$ be positive. Set $t=(2m+1)/(m+1)$. If $(t-1)^kB\le M^{2/t}$ and
$M\le A^{2-t}B^{t-1}$, then
\[
B\le\left((1+1/m)^{m+1}\right)^{2k}A^2.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Limit of the finite degree factors]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.degree_norm_limit}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $k$, the sequence $\bigl((1+1/m)^{m+1}\bigr)^{2k}$, indexed by
natural numbers $m$, converges to $e^{2k}$ as $m$ tends to infinity.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Endpoint of a family of norm comparisons]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.degree_norm_endpoint}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.degree_norm_limit}
\difficulty{1}
Let $k$ be a nonnegative integer and let $A,B\in\mathbb R$. Suppose that for every
integer $m\ge2$, $B\le\bigl((1+1/m)^{m+1}\bigr)^{2k}A^2$. Then $B\le e^{2k}A^2$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.low_degree_l1_l2_sq}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n,k$ be natural numbers, and let $p$ be a coefficient family on the subsets of the
$n$ coordinates, with $p(S)=0$ whenever $|S|>k$. If
$P(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}p(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S$ is the Walsh
character, then $\displaystyle
e^{-2k}\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}p(S)^2\leq\left(\mathbb
E_{x\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\{0,1\}^n)}|P(x)|\right)^2$.
\end{theorem}
